summary: On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu formally rejected the U.S.-backed 15-point Gaza reconstruction plan, insisting the Israel Defense Forces will not withdraw until Hamas is 'genuinely' disarmed.

Sequencing remains a primary point of contention, as the roadmap proposes phased Israeli withdrawal parallel to Hamas disarmament, whereas Netanyahu countered that Israel requires 'genuine disarmament, not fictitious disarmament' of all weaponry.

Facing razor-tight elections on October 27, Netanyahu is under mounting pressure from his far-right coalition, with National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir dismissing the draft as 'not acceptable' to shore up his political base.

Hamas remains committed to the roadmap and urges mediators to pressure Netanyahu to adhere to the plan, while health officials report more than 1,250 Palestinians killed since the ceasefire began amid continuing military strikes.

The rare public break tests President Donald Trump's relationship with Netanyahu, who previously hailed the plan as a 'monumental step toward lasting peace,' leaving the roadmap's future uncertain as electoral considerations override diplomatic efforts.
title: Source Icon

summary: Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg issued a high-priority memo giving defense contractors 21 days to submit plans for accelerating production schedules and expanding capacity. Declaring that "years-long development cycles are not acceptable," the directive targets critical capabilities to replenish heavily depleted munitions stockpiles.

The surge comes amid severe strain on air defense inventories due to ongoing conflict with Iran. According to an analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies , U.S. stockpiles of Patriot interceptors have dropped by over 65% , while THAAD interceptor stocks have fallen by roughly 38%.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell confirmed the authenticity of the memo, stating that the initiative aligns with efforts to rebuild the defense industrial base and will directly inform the fiscal year 2028 defense budget submission.

The directive follows pushback from President Donald Trump, who publicly rejected reports of weapons shortages on Truth Social, insisting the U.S. has "massive amounts" of munitions being actively manufactured and delivered.

Efforts to ramp up procurement face legislative headwinds, as a defense spending bill remains stalled in Congress over disagreements regarding White House requests to raise Pentagon funding to $1.5 trillion.
title: Pentagon pushes defense companies to boost weapons production after concerns of depleted stocks

summary: The Senate voted 50–49 to confirm Todd Blanche as U.S. Attorney General, ending a contentious confirmation fight and officially installing President Donald Trump's former criminal defense lawyer atop the Department of Justice.
Sen. Bill Cassidy provided the decisive swing vote after declaring his support on the floor, while Republican Sens. Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski joined all Democrats in opposing the nomination.

The pre-dawn 4:31 a.m. vote took place immediately before the Senate adjourned for a five-week recess, granting Blanche full confirmation after serving in an acting capacity since Trump removed former AG Pam Bondi in April.

Confirmation prospects were stalled for weeks over a controversial $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization fund" and tax immunity provisions stemming from a DOJ settlement with Trump over his leaked IRS records.

Blanche secured key Republican votes by offering written assurances, officially rescinding the payout fund and clarifying that tax audit immunity applied only to existing claims and did not protect against future tax filings.
title: Senate narrowly approves Todd Blanche as AG, capping tough confirmation fight

summary: On Saturday, the Senate approved a short-term funding measure by a 90-6 vote to fund federal agencies through Dec. 11, averting a potentially chaotic government shutdown during campaign season.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune prioritized the deal nearly two months before the Sept. 30 fiscal deadline to allow senators a five-week recess for reelection campaigns, still recovering from two historic shutdowns this past year.

Senator Susan Collins, R-Maine, and Democrats negotiated provisions blocking new grant regulations opposed by nearly 500,000 public commenters, while also preventing Border Patrol transfers and rejecting the White House's $1 billion battleship request.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer attacked the battleship proposal, saying "The only person who wants these golden ships is Donald Trump so he can slap his name on them," while the White House Office of Management and Budget defended its grant review as improving accountability.

The bill retains a one-month delay on intoxicating hemp products despite Senator Ted Budd's unsuccessful effort to strip it, citing a nearly 10-fold increase in cannabis emergency room visits by minors since 2017; the House must approve when members return from recess.
title: U.S. Senate passes short-term funding bill to avert federal shutdown before election

summary: President Donald Trump renewed his attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday, reviving an effort the Supreme Court blocked in June to preserve the central bank's independence.

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino sent a letter dated August 5 to Cook, stating the President is "considering" her removal due to unproven mortgage fraud allegations raised by Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency.

The Supreme Court's 5-4 ruling in June blocked the initial firing, finding Trump failed to provide procedural protections; the White House now demands Cook respond within 21 days to satisfy the court's mandate.

Cook, the first Black woman to serve as a Federal Reserve governor, denied wrongdoing and maintained the allegations are "a manufactured pretext" for monetary policy differences, noting she has not been charged with any crime.

Chief Justice John Roberts warned in the June opinion that allowing the President to fire Cook "would in effect transform the Federal Reserve's for-cause protection into at-will employment," undermining the Nation's central banking independence from political pressure.
title: Trump Moving Forward with Attempt to Fire Fed's Lisa Cook After Supreme Court Ruling

summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday directing federal health agencies to overhaul childhood vaccine recommendations and reduce the number of vaccines routinely recommended for all children.
The order calls for vaccines to be administered individually rather than in combination when possible, including splitting the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine into three separate shots.

The revised recommendations would broadly recommend vaccines against 11 diseases instead of 17, while moving protections against several diseases, including influenza, hepatitis A and B, and some forms of meningitis, to high-risk or shared-decision categories.
Trump repeatedly linked the changes to concerns about autism, suggesting that the increase in childhood vaccinations could be related to rising autism diagnoses.

The order represents a major shift in federal vaccine policy under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., while medical and public-health experts have warned that weakening routine recommendations could reduce vaccination rates and leave children more vulnerable to preventable diseases.
title: Trump signs executive order aimed at reducing number of recommended childhood vaccines

summary: On Monday, the Indiana Recount Commission declared Paula Copenhaver the winner of Senate District 23, overturning the primary results by a three-vote margin and unseating incumbent Republican Sen. Spencer Deery.

State law requires absentee ballots to bear the county clerk's signature and initials from both Republican and Democratic election judges; the commission rejected eight ballots for Deery and two for Copenhaver for lacking these credentials.

Deery's counsel, Samantha DeWester, plans to appeal the decision to the Indiana Court of Appeals as the recount reflects a broader trend: seven of eight Republican state senators opposing redistricting lost their primaries this year.

Senate District 23 stretches from western Tippecanoe and Montgomery counties to the Illinois border, a region where Deery held the presumptive lead before Monday's recount action overturned the outcome.

Sen. Greg Goode, R-Terre Haute, remains the sole survivor among eight Republican state senators who voted against redistricting, as the commission's ruling finalizes a sweep of primary defeats for those who opposed the measure.
title: Recount Flips Indiana Senate District 23 Win to Paula Copenhaver

Mace wrote on Friday that every Muslim official is a "trojan horse," explicitly targeting Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and activist Hasan Piker.

Critics and former officials condemned the remarks on social media, while Mace maintained her position, echoing rhetoric she previously used during the South Carolina Republican gubernatorial primary campaign.

High-Profile violent crimes prompted the federal intervention, including the 2024 killing of former Trump administration official Mike Gill and the June 2025 death of congressional intern Eric Tarpinian in a crossfire shooting.

Law enforcement made more than 16,000 arrests, including 35 homicide suspects and more than 100 gang members, while overall crime fell 20% in the last year, with motor vehicle thefts dropping 53% and homicide rates declining 32%.

Approximately 4,600 National Guard troops remain stationed in D.C., though Mayor Muriel Bowser questioned the deployment's legality, and the mission has resulted in casualties including West Virginia National Guard member Sarah Beckstrom's death.

The Department of War estimates extending the National Guard deployment through January 2029 could cost $1.4 billion, as the administration continues clearing homeless encampments and constructing monuments honoring the nation's 250th anniversary.

The White House publicly maintained that Trump traveled on the older 747, which he had promised to fly "for old time's sake," though the operation successfully fooled journalists on the decoy aircraft.

This operation follows previous security measures where aides used a decoy plane owned by ally Steve Witkoff to protect the president, a tactic so tightly held that it fooled even people traveling with him.
title: Trump flew secretly from Turkey due to Iranian threat, The Washington Post reports

The clash took place during a discussion marking the first anniversary of a CDC shooting linked to COVID-19 vaccine misinformation, honoring Officer David Rose who died protecting CDC employees.
Bhattacharya accused the Biden administration of censoring him and challenged Brennan's focus on the shooter, emphasizing a broader loss of trust caused by partial perspectives during the pandemic.
The White House criticized Brennan's interview, accusing mainstream media of lacking humility and worsening public trust in health bodies.

New evidence from Bedfordshire police led to serious pending charges in Britain involving human trafficking and violent rapes against multiple victims, while a separate case in Romania remains stalled due to ongoing procedural problems.

Attorneys filed a motion Friday arguing the brothers' high profile makes flight nearly impossible and that they have complied with all pretrial restrictions during previous legal proceedings in Romania.
A detention hearing scheduled for Thursday in Miami will determine whether the Tates remain jailed or are released during what could be a monthslong international extradition process.

While the Tates have amassed over 10 million followers and are vocal supporters of President Donald Trump, The White House stated the brothers should not expect any presidential assistance regarding their legal situation.
title: US prosecutors want Tate brothers to remain in custody as they fight extradition to the UK

summary: Embattled Republican Rep. Max Miller announced he will remain in the race for Ohio 's 7th Congressional District, defying calls from party figures to withdraw amid scrutiny of domestic abuse allegations from his ex-wife, Emily Moreno.
While Sen. Bernie Moreno urged him to withdraw, Miller retains support from President Donald Trump, who called him "a good person" and dismissed the legal dispute as a family matter.

Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters said on Sunday, "Everybody has to prove they are capable of winning," as Miller reported plans to invest $1 million of his own capital into his campaign.
Democratic challenger Brian Poindexter is capitalizing on the controversy, securing union endorsements from the United Auto Workers and AFSCME while promising to "serve with honor" to attract voters.
Miller won the seat with 51% of the vote two years ago in a three-way contest, though he acknowledged the president warned it would be "a tough race" in the 55%-44% Republican-leaning district.
title: Deadline passes for Rep. Max Miller to be replaced on Ohio ballot as he faces domestic abuse claims

summary: On Monday, former Northern Arizona University fraternity leader Carter Thomas Eslick pleaded guilty to felony hazing in connection with the January 30 death of 18-year-old pledge Colin Daniel Martinez in Flagstaff.

During an invite-only Delta Tau Delta rush event, Eslick directed pledges to play a drinking game where they were given a "handle of vodka" to consume together, exposing Martinez to substantial risk of death.
An autopsy confirmed Martinez died from alcohol poisoning, with his blood-alcohol level reaching 0.425%, more than five times the legal limit; officers discovered vodka and Twisted Teas at the scene.
The university suspended the Delta Tau Delta chapter and the national organization closed the NAU branch, while Eslick faces sentencing on September 30 where a judge will determine his penalty.

Regardless of the final sentence, Eslick faces fines up to $150,000 and must pay restitution to the Martinez family, as Coconino County Attorney Ammon Barker noted the plea does not diminish the "profound harm caused or the sorrow of Colin's death.
title: Ex-fraternity member pleads guilty to hazing an Arizona university pledge to death

summary: Amazon is developing a data center campus in Pecos County, Texas, featuring an on-site natural gas power plant permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide annually, potentially making it the country's largest single source of climate pollution.

High demand for artificial intelligence has triggered a data center boom, with facilities seeking 474 gigawatts of electricity—approximately 90 percent of new power requests on the Texas grid—prompting tech companies to invest in fossil fuel sources.

The United States has at least 82 data center-linked gas generators in development, which could collectively emit enough carbon dioxide in one year to rival the output of half the passenger cars in the country.

Republican Governor Greg Abbott paused new data center projects in Texas this week, ordering state regulators to audit proposed facilities because, as he stated, "Texans must come first" regarding grid capacity.

Amazon said it is "exploring opportunities for solar energy and battery storage on site" while backing 40 renewable projects in Texas and designing the Pecos facility to transition to grid-connected service eventually.
title: Amazon behind massive private gas plant for new data centers

summary: On Monday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and officials renamed Joint Base Charleston to Joint Base Lindsey Graham in South Carolina, honoring the late senator's military and public service legacy.

Graham, a longtime Republican from South Carolina, died last month at age 71 following an aortic dissection; his sister, Senator Darline Graham, attended the ceremony to honor his 33 years of service to the United States.
During the ceremony, Hegseth urged Congress to support the Pentagon's massive budget request of $1.5 trillion, a sharp increase from the roughly $800 million approved for last year.
Hegseth criticized "woke, so-called leaders" of the military during his speech, yet Republicans remain skeptical of the $1.5 trillion request amid the ongoing war with Iran.
The renamed installation hosts the 628th Air Base Wing, covers nearly 24,000 acres, and supports more than 90,000 personnel including airmen, sailors, soldiers, and civilians.
title: Pentagon renames South Carolina air base after Graham

Across 142 episodes from 1979 to 1985, Jones portrayed Hazzard County mechanic Cooter Davenport; he later owned Cooter's Place, a themed store with locations in Nashville, Pigeon Forge, and Luray.
From 1989 to 1993, Jones represented Georgia's Fourth Congressional District outside Atlanta after winning his 1988 House race by 20 points.
Co-Star Tom Wopat paid tribute on Instagram, writing that Jones was 'a fine friend and a fierce advocate' and an 'integral part' of the cast.
A reunion event in Luray had been planned to celebrate Jones alongside cast member Sonny Enos Shroyer, who turns 91 on August 28.
title: Ben Jones, Good Ol' Boy 'Dukes of Hazzard' Actor and 2-Term US House Member, Dies at 84

summary: Testimony resumed Monday in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, Massachusetts mother, with defense attorney Kevin Reddington beginning his cross-examination of Dr. Jennifer Tufts, the psychiatrist who treated Clancy before the 2023 killings at Plymouth Superior Court.

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington contends that Clancy suffered from undiagnosed postpartum psychosis and received improper medication, while prosecutors argue she was aware of her actions when she killed her three children in January 2023.

The defense noted that Clancy received 30 prescriptions for 13 drugs from at least six providers between September 2022 and the January 2023 deaths, while questioning Tufts about the 14 telemedicine visits she conducted.

While Tufts testified she observed no signs of psychosis during her sessions, Dr. Veerle Bergink, director of the Women's Mental Health Center at Mount Sinai, said multiple providers missed Clancy's diagnosis.

Clancy alleges a "catastrophic failure" of multiple medical providers in diagnosing and treating her psychiatric condition, as Reddington continues arguing her mental state left her unable to distinguish right from wrong.

summary: On Monday, the Wisconsin Department of Justice identified Madison Police Department officer Kiel Baitinger-Peterson as the officer who fatally shot 38-year-old Corey Ruiz on July 22 during an attempted arrest on Williamson Street.

Responding to reports of vehicle tampering and attempted burglary, four officers confronted Ruiz, who fled on a bicycle before a physical struggle ensued where officials say Ruiz "brandished a knife and injured" Baitinger-Peterson.

Before the shooting, two other officers attempted to use a Taser on Ruiz "without success," while Baitinger-Peterson, with nearly 11 years of experience, fired the fatal shots as bystanders captured the struggle on cellphone video.

All four involved officers were placed on paid administrative leave pending the state investigation. City workers cleared a protest encampment at the shooting site last Tuesday, resulting in several arrests.

Civil rights attorney Ben Crump, representing the Ruiz family, has called for charges against the officer. Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway plans to include funding for body-worn cameras in the next budget for the Madison Police Department.
title: Authorities ID the Officer Who Fatally Shot a Black Man on a Bike in Madison, Wisconsin

College athletes face increased vulnerability due to high social media exposure and NIL-related status, which hackers leverage to steal private data, sell images, or blackmail victims.
Former Michigan staffer Matt Weiss allegedly hacked more than 3,300 accounts of college athletes, while the FBI fields more than 3,000 tips daily about cyber sexual exploitation victims.
The NCAA will serve as an informational liaison, providing educational resources and connecting impacted athletes with FBI victim advocates and counseling support services.
"We hope to break down barriers," NCAA Vice President of Enforcement Jon Duncan said, ensuring athletes feel comfortable seeking help to prevent further abuse.
title: FBI Teams with the NCAA to Help Athletes Avoid Sexual Exploitation

summary: The Charity Commission launched a statutory inquiry yesterday into the Croydon-based Al-Khair Foundation to investigate alleged links to Hamas . Regulators are assessing whether trustees exercised adequate due diligence on partners and the use of funds.

Following the July 31 arrest of Turkish national Mohammad Yousef Hasna, Counter Terror Policing London executed two search warrants at addresses in Croydon. Prosecutors allege Hasna conspired to funnel money and supplies to Hamas through a sham humanitarian organization.

Hasna, 45, faces United States charges of conspiring to finance terrorism, with each count carrying a maximum 20-year prison sentence. The Al-Khair Foundation is subject to a legal order restricting certain financial transactions without Charity Commission consent.
The Al-Khair Foundation stated it is "co-operating fully" with the inquiry and maintains that Hasna is not an employee but works with one of its global partners to deliver aid in Gaza.

Reporting more than £74 million in income for the financial year ending July 31, 2025, the foundation's substantial revenue underscores the inquiry's significance. Regulators must determine whether trustees conducted proper due diligence on partners and charitable resource allocation.
title: UK Charity Probed Over Hamas Financing Links

summary: On Tuesday, Jonathan Veitch, head of UNICEF for the Palestinian territories, reported that Israeli water infrastructure restrictions are squandering Canadian aid, citing destruction of the Canada Well facility.

Israel restricts items like cement and generators as 'dual-use' materials to prevent Hamas from building weapons, forcing UNICEF to become the 'provider of last resort' for water and sanitation services across Gaza.

Veitch described dire conditions where families live in makeshift tents surrounded by waste, with nighttime temperatures seldom dropping below 25 C and "millions and millions of rats" infesting the area.
The Israeli Defense Forces stated last week it is assessing infrastructure damage with severity, while 2.1 million Gazans remain confined to 30 per cent of the territory facing critical shortages.

Canada "punches above its weight" in humanitarian assistance, Veitch said, noting private donations helped end a recent famine, though he warned peace remains elusive as thousands grow up without education.
title: UNICEF Official Says Gaza Water Restrictions Waste Canadian Aid

summary: On Tuesday, Wisconsin voters head to the polls to select a Democratic nominee for governor, concluding a chaotic primary after candidates made final pitches Monday to replace outgoing Governor Tony Evers.
Evers' decision not to seek a third term created an open race that initially featured seven Democrats, which narrowed significantly following campaign scandals and candidate withdrawals.

Hong, a democratic socialist, has tapped into party anger, while Evers endorsed Crowley, citing his experience leading the state's most populous county; Madison State Senator Kelda Roys and Department of Administration Secretary Joel Brennan also compete.

To defeat Republican U.S. Representative Tom Tiffany in November, Democrats are calling for unity, as Crowley urged supporters to "come together after the primary" to ensure a MAGA extremist does not occupy the governor's office.

Beyond the gubernatorial race, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's son-in-law, Michael Alfonso, competes in a five-way Republican primary for Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District, as Democrats aim to capitalize on low Trump approval ratings to flip the Legislature.
title: Democratic Socialist Tries to Beat Governor’s Pick in Chaotic Wisconsin Primary for Governor

summary: On Sunday, Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed told CNN he would use subpoena powers to investigate Trump administration officials, including RFK Jr., if elected as part of a Democratic Senate majority.

The 41-year-old epidemiologist defeated Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens in last week's primary, securing the Democratic nomination and drawing endorsements from Bernie Sanders and the American Federation of Government Employees .

AFGE's endorsement reflects a broader shift toward political advocacy, with El-Sayed promoting Medicare and antitrust enforcement; critics argue such union moves risk alienating members with differing political views.
If elected, El-Sayed's Medicare platform would replace the Federal Employees Health Benefits program, altering negotiated plan designs and provider networks for federal workers.

While El-Sayed rejects the 'socialist' label, stating he 'believe in capitalism,' his platform aligns with Democratic Socialists priorities including the PRO Act, creating ongoing debate over his political identity.
title: Abdul El-Sayed Vows to Hold Trump Administration Accountable if Democrats Win Senate

summary: President Donald Trump 's foreign real-estate licensing revenue reached $59.5 million in 2025, a 71% increase from 2024, driven by new licensing LLCs concentrated in Gulf projects across developers like Saudi-linked Dar Al Arkan and UAE-based Damac.
This surge follows the Trump Organization's reversal of its first-term pledge to pursue "no new foreign deals whatsoever," with four new licensing LLCs accounting for 82% of the increase.

More than 60% of the income originated from Gulf projects, including $25.8 million tied to Dar Global and $11.3 million from Damac-linked developments, with previously inactive LLCs generating an additional $9.64 million.

Ethics experts including Kedric Payne, ethics director at the Campaign Legal Center, warn the deals create an "appearance of an ethics problem" and raise unresolved questions about the Constitution's Foreign Emoluments Clause.

A Damac subsidiary paid $36.5 million for Ohio land near Canton in December while the administration concurrently accelerated permitting for data centers, prompting critics to question whether business ties influence official policy decisions.
title: Trump’s foreign licensing business booms to $59.5 million as Gulf developers pay

summary: On Saturday, the Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as Attorney General in a 50-49 vote, ending a lengthy standoff between Senate Republicans and the Trump administration over the appointment of President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer.

Opposition centered on Blanche's previous experience as a defense attorney and a proposed $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization' fund meant to compensate 'victims of government persecution,' which critics feared would benefit those prosecuted for the January 6 attack.

Louisiana Republican Senator Bill Cassidy cast the deciding vote for confirmation, despite acknowledging Blanche's 'poor judgment in approving the anti-weaponization slush fund and exempting the president from IRS audits,' while GOP Senators Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski voted against him.

Although Department of Justice officials stated they have 'rescinded' the controversial fund, Democrats contend the department's written agreements with Senator John Cornyn are merely 'decorative' and do not guarantee the fund is permanently abandoned.

summary: On Monday, Intel announced a $15 billion common stock offering to fund its chip contract manufacturing turnaround and meet skyrocketing demand for artificial intelligence compute.
Seeking to challenge TSMC, Intel is investing in new facilities and advanced packaging while capitalizing on a stock rally that has seen shares more than double this year.

JPMorgan Securities, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup Global Markets are managing the sale, which includes a 30-day option for underwriters to purchase up to $2.25 billion in additional shares.
Intel shares fell more than 3% in premarket trading, reflecting investor concerns regarding potential shareholder dilution from the stock sale.
Goldman estimates capital expenditures on artificial intelligence demand will reach $765 billion this year and $1.2 trillion in 2027, as tech giants continue scaling infrastructure.
title: Intel launches $15 billion share sale as turnaround rally lifts stock
